rationale: Base station HB-200 is online with uplink_status "ok" and all 7 devices online locally, yet E-503 "cloud reporting failed repeatedly" persists. The standard L1 fix (power-cycle base station + confirm automatic DNS) was attempted and failed, and the KB explicitly states E-503 persisting while the base station is online requires FAE escalation (cloud channel or certificate issue, matching historical case H-06). The customer's mesh Wi-Fi change is not the cause since local uplink and streaming work fine.

Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

The base station connects to the home router by Ethernet (recommended) or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. If all cameras and sensors show offline in the app at the same time, first check whether the base station itself is online. Power-cycle the router, wait 2 minutes, then power-cycle the base station. The base station requires outbound TCP 443 and 8883 to the cloud.

complaint: My cameras work locally, but remote notifications have stopped. We just got a new mesh Wi-Fi system and I wonder if it blocks something. I've disabled the firewall features in the mesh app and rebooted all the nodes. Our old router is in a drawer if I should plug it back in.
usability_reason: The response is clear and polite, accurately summarizes the symptom and the one L1 step the customer actually performed (power-cycle plus DNS confirmation), and correctly notes it failed. It avoids claiming unperformed checks or fixes, and gives an actionable next step (escalation with a timeframe). It loses a point because the customer's mesh-Wi-Fi/old-router question is not directly addressed, and the suspected root cause (certificate/backend) is speculative rather than confirmed, though it is framed as suspected and tied to a historical case rather than asserted as completed.
